correctness.rationale: For a fixed shift, after the highest shift bit the carry survives across h further bits only on a cylinder of frequency 2^(-h); one more bit accounts for the last adjacent pair. Finite cylinders have natural frequencies on all initial integer intervals, so taking the cutoff to infinity establishes the natural law without loss of mass. The identity r(4q+b)=r(q)+floor(b/2)(q mod 2)+[b=3] gives the stated parity recurrences. At shift 1, the even case flips a low zero; the odd case with h trailing ones loses h-1 pairs and gains the bit above the first zero. Its geometric law gives the stated starting functions. For the Mersenne shifts T_k, B_{T_k}=H for k>=3 follows from the power-of-two laws, and A_{T_{k+1}}=(z A_{T_k}+H)/2. The negative terms of these functions arise solely from c/(2z-1): the numerator value at z=1/2. In this recurrence c maps to c/4+(27/64)/2, and the length-four initial value 9/32 is exactly the fixed point. The increments therefore have polynomial support, also after multiplication by 1+z. Doubling an odd shift gives the displayed boundary weighting; further doublings leave the law unchanged by the 4u recursion. The negative masses of the weighted length-four terms are 27/64 and 73/64; the latter adds H's constant coefficient 19/64 to twice its negative mass. These facts give both infinite plateaus. An independent exact carry enumeration checked all six boundary values and the plateau for k=4..10 at j=0..3, giving both rows and the claimed strict minimum/equality comparison.
residual_risks: The finite independent check is not a proof of the infinite plateau; that follows from the fixed point and support argument. No assertion for multiple runs or convergence rate is warranted.
